Praise of the Buddha, the Blessed One, from the *Praśastapraśaṃsā*, titled "The Praise that Generates Weariness with Existence," being the twelfth chapter.

The *Praise of the Praiseworthy*, a hymn of praise to the Buddha, the Blessed One, composed by the master Mañjuśrīmitra, is hereby complete. It was translated, edited, and finalized by the Indian preceptor Sarvajñādeva and the chief editor-translator, the monk Dpal brtsegs rakṣita.
Inducing Aversion Toward Saṃsāra (*Vav*).

Sanskrit: Hartmann (1987). Tibetan: Sarvajñādeva et al. (chapters 1–12) and Padmākara et al. (chapter 13), Hartmann (1987) 13,1–Tibetan: Sarvajñādeva et al. (chapters 1–12) and Padmākara et al. (chapter 13), Hartmann (1987) 15.
Relying upon you, who possess great fortune for composing poetry, my intellect shall increase exceedingly, even though it is small,
like a river in the summer season.
Relying upon you, the most distinguished among poets (*kāvya-kāra*), my own imagination, though small, swells greatly like a river in the summer [monsoon].
Having obtained this difficult-to-find gain and having acquired this tongue,
who would not act for their own benefit by proclaiming the virtues of the Protector?
Having attained this human rebirth so difficult to find and this very tongue, who would not bring benefit to themselves by proclaiming the qualities of the Protector?
Your body, adorned with the marks, is beautiful— a nectar for the eyes—
resembling the cloudless autumn sky adorned by a host of stars.
Your body, adorned with the marks (*lakṣaṇa*), beautiful and nectar for the eyes, is like the cloudless autumn sky adorned by the hosts of stars.
The Sage, possessing a golden complexion and beautified by his dharma robes,
resembles the peak of a golden mountain enveloped by the clouds of twilight.

With a body the color of gold, silent, and enveloped in the saffron robe, you are beautiful, like the peak of a golden mountain encircled by clouds in its midst. Protector, though you are not adorned with ornaments, the radiance of your facial disk does not exist even in the full orb of the moon when it is free from clouds.
O Protector, though you are not adorned with ornaments, even the orb of the moon, full and free from clouds, does not possess the brilliance that your face possesses.
When bees behold your lotus-face and a lotus opened by the sun,
they will take hold of the lotus, their doubts hanging in suspense.
When the bees see the lotus of your face and a lotus opened by the sun, they seize the rope of doubt as to which is the true lotus. Your face, possessing a golden hue,
with its beautiful white teeth, resembles the stainless moonbeams of autumn entering the midst of a mountain of gold.

The beauty of your white teeth in your golden face is like the stainless radiance of the autumn moon upon the Golden Mountain (Meru). O Worthy One, your right hand, adorned with the mark of the wheel, grants consolation with its touch to those terrified by cyclic existence.
Your right hand, O Venerable One, adorned with the mark (*lakṣaṇa*) of the wheel, bestows consolation upon those beings who are terrified by cyclic existence (*saṃsāra*).
When you, the Sage, set out, this earth was marked by your two feet, which resembled glorious lotuses; how beautiful it was, as if covered in lotuses!
When you began to walk, Śvager, this place was painted by your two feet, which resemble the lotus of fortune, and it became beautiful as if possessed by lotus flowers (or: like Padmāvatī).
You walked with that incomparable gait—steadier than a rutting noble elephant, or a female swan, or even a bull.
Your gait is incomparable; whether it be a rutting state elephant or a male rhinoceros with its mate, you stride more firmly than even a bull (*ṛṣabha*).

With a body vast through the aggregate of ethical discipline, adorned by the tree of meditative concentration, and pervaded by the falling waters of primordial wisdom—you are a moving mountain of snow.

Your body, vast with the mountain peaks (*kūṭa*) of ethical discipline (*śīla*), adorned with the trees of meditative concentration (*samādhi*), and permeated by the streams of primordial wisdom (*jñāna*), is a moving Himālaya. Whoever touches your body, O ocean of qualities, has thereby created a bathing ghat (*tīrtha*) to be honored by gods and humans.

O Ocean of Qualities, you transform all who touch you with their bodies into a sacred bathing place (*tīrtha*) venerated by gods and humans. Since even the sight of your abode— a field of accomplishment— purifies the mind, what need is there for the wise who desire purity to resort to foul-smelling [ascetic] practices?
Your dwelling place is the field of the perfected ones; having seen this and become pure in mind, what remains for the wise who long for purity there to be a field of harsh words?
You are perfectly beautiful, endowed with the six perfections, like the full moon adorned by the Pleiades.

Exceedingly beautiful through the possession of the six perfections (*pāramitā*), you are like the full moon adorned with the Pleiades. You awaken the lotuses of those beings to be trained who were asleep, just as the rising sun causes the lotuses to bloom.
You awaken the person to be subdued, like a lotus from its sleep, just as the risen sun causes a lotus to open.

Vav San: Hartmann (1987) – San: Hartmann (1987) Vav Tib: Sarvajñādeva et al. (chs. 1–12) and Padmākara et al. (ch. 13), Hartmann (1987) 13,16 – Tib: Sarvajñādeva et al. (chs. 1–12) and Padmākara et al. (ch. 13), Hartmann (1987) 32
To those seized by the poison of the afflictions, you grant the medicine of primordial wisdom;
just as the Protector of Beings removes the venom from one bitten by a fanged serpent.

To those who are consumed by the poison of the afflictions (*kleśa*), you grant the medicine of wisdom; this is like the removal of poison from those seized by venomous serpents by means of *’gro-skyob*.
Your forest fire of primordial wisdom has incinerated the net of views, just as a fiercely blazing forest fire consumes the saplings of trees.
The forest fire of your wisdom has consumed the net of false views (*dṛṣṭijāla*); this is like a brightly blazing forest fire that consumes the branches and twigs of trees.
By means of the blazing nature of your wisdom, O Sage, you dry up the mire of the afflictions (*kleśa*);
this is equal to the radiance of the sun.

O Śveta, you who dry up the mire of defilements with the radiant sun of your wisdom—this is like the light of the sun. By your speech, you turn the minds of men away from what is improper; this is like a great charioteer turning back a wayward elephant with his lasso.

Your words restrain the minds of people from what should not be done; this is like the charioteer’s rein that holds back a cow from wandering astray. Even if you alone were liberated from the bonds of the afflictions, you would still become worthy of worship for the sake of liberating others; thus, you are preeminently worthy of honor.
If there is anyone worthy of hope, you alone are such; for having been liberated from the fetters of the afflictions and having subsequently liberated others as well, you are universally venerable.
By the light-rays of your speech, you satisfy those scorched by the afflictions, just as the moonbeams of night soothe the heat of summer.

With the rays of light from your words, you refresh those tormented by the defilements, just as the rays of the night moon refresh those tormented by the summer heat. To the beings who are to be trained, your face— contemplating the Dharma— is like a mass of monsoon clouds to a traveler parched with thirst.

When those to be tamed, tormented by thirst for the Dharma, behold your face, they are like the cātaka bird, tormented by thirst, beholding the masses of summer rain clouds. Your speech, with the sound of the Dharma, brings joy to all who are to be tamed; it is like the sound of a melodious song that even causes the deer to stand still.

Your words delight all who are to be tamed with the resonance of the Dharma; this is like the deer that, though they are in motion, are brought to stillness by the sound of a lovely melody. Those seeking refuge who ought to seek refuge do not go to you for refuge; those who take refuge in non-Buddhist extremists will suffer for a long time without protection.
If those seeking refuge do not take refuge in you, the Worthy One of Refuge, but instead take refuge in false teachers, they will suffer for a long time without refuge.
Even though Śakra does not perceive reality with his thousand eyes,
you see it with the eye of primordial wisdom and reveal it to others as well.

That ultimate reality (*tattva*) which even Indra was unable to see despite his thousand eyes— you behold it with the eye of wisdom and furthermore teach it to others. O you who possess the certainty of realization regarding the treatises, the many disputants, upon seeing you, become dejected and wander about like bees.

The numerous disputants, proud of their precise mastery of the treatises, become disheartened in your presence and buzz about like bees. When you defeat your opponents with even a single word, others remain in a state of silence, like cuckoos in winter.
When an opponent has already been utterly defeated by even a single word of yours, the others remain in a state of speechlessness, like the cuckoo in winter.
Your excellent disciples are like a tree in springtime, beautiful and adorned with flowers, as their virtuous blossoms flourish most abundantly.
The tree of your excellent disciples, overflowing with the flowers of the wholesome, is as beautiful as a tree in spring adorned with blossoms.
O Sage, the arrow of your wisdom has pierced the target of all that is knowable;
in the city of Rāmagrāma, even the master archer did not pierce it before you.

The arrow of your insight, O Silent One, has struck the mark of the knowable; in the city of Ga-byed (?), it was not struck before by gZu-rgyal (?). Those arrogant with the conceit of being wise, because they do not know the path to liberation, wander through the wilderness of existence; they are like a multitude of blind people in a vast, empty desert.
Because those who possess the vain pride of learning do not seek your path to liberation, they wander through the wilderness of existence like herds of blind men in an uninhabited land.
As for the worldly, they give rise to doubt, wondering whether actions bear fruit or not; yet you are the very embodiment of the sovereign power of virtuous deeds.
Ordinary worldly beings harbor doubts as to whether actions will bear fruit or not; yet, through the power of your virtuous deeds, your body has become thus.
O Ocean of Qualities, I cannot fathom the limit of your qualities;
it is like a bird being unable to reach the end of the sky, which is the color of blue lapis lazuli.
O Ocean of Qualities, I do not perceive the end of your qualities, just as birds do not perceive the end of the sapphire-blue color of the sky.
